title: Laptop overheating and shutting down
symptom: Laptop gets very hot, fan is loud, and it shuts itself off
user_description: My laptop gets really hot and the fan sounds like a jet engine. Then it just switches itself off in the middle of work.

options.text: Disable the overheating shutdown so it keeps running
options.why: The shutdown exists to protect the hardware from heat damage. Removing it risks permanent damage and lost data.

options.text: Check the vents are clear of dust and blocked airflow, use it on a hard flat surface, and look in Task Manager for a program using the CPU constantly
options.why: Blocked vents and soft surfaces trap heat, and a program stuck at full CPU makes the laptop run hot. These are the most common and cheapest causes to check.
Drastic and unlikely to fix a heat problem. It could only help if software is the cause, and nobody has checked that.

options.text: Run it with the bottom panel removed for extra cooling
options.why: Exposes internal parts to dust and damage, and it does not fix the real cause. Never run hardware with covers removed.

hints: Is the laptop running hot because of what it is doing, or because it cannot get rid of heat?
Where does a laptop's hot air leave, and what could block it?
Which tool shows what is using the processor all the time?
real_world_tip: Ask where he uses it. Laptops on beds, sofas and car seats cover their air vents and overheat quickly.
